findings.label: M1
findings.text:
The hint prints the path raw inside a copy-paste shell command, so a hostile or odd file name can inject output and shell syntax (`skills/project-update/update.py:1250-1254`)  in_scope: yes
why it matters: I reproduced this in a scratch repo. I tracked `.ai/state/n<LF>l; touch pwn #.jsonl` (it matches `.ai/state/*.jsonl`). The report printed a fake `hint` continuation line, followed by `git rm --cached -- .ai/state/n<LF>l; touch pwn #.jsonl` inside backticks. A path with a space (`a b.jsonl`) also prints a command that untracks the wrong paths (`.ai/state/a` and `b.jsonl`). Anyone who clones a repo can plant such a name, and the output is read by an agent and a human. SKILL.md tells the agent to relay `git rm --cached -- <path>` to the human. The `-z` parsing is correct, but it makes the raw bytes reach stdout and the command line. The change declares "no crash", and it does not crash, but the printed command is wrong or unsafe for any name that needs quoting.
suggested direction: Build the command with `shlex.quote(path)`. Escape control characters in the display (for example `repr`-style or `\n`) so a name cannot start a new `hint` line. Add one test case with a space in the name and one with a newline.

findings.label: L1
findings.text:
The test never exercises a path that needs quoting, and it does not cover a project root that is a subdirectory of a work tree or `--apply` (`tests/test_project_update.py:1428-1461`)  in_scope: yes
why it matters: M1 would pass this test. The test covers the main case (positive hint, `--check` exit 0, negative after `git rm --cached`, and no git at all), and the negative case is real: the file stays on disk and is ignored. I ran the subdirectory case by hand and it works, because `ls-files` paths are relative to `-C root`. That case is unpinned. "`--apply` writes nothing for it" is also unpinned, although the code adds no plan item. My manual `--apply` run and a rerun gave exit 0 and "up to date".
suggested direction: Add the subdirectory-root and odd-name assertions to the same test, if cheap. The test's `self.env` copies the whole `os.environ`, so a stray `GIT_DIR` would leak in. This is the same as the existing git tests, so it is not blocking.

findings.label: L2
findings.text:
The wording says "ignored by .gitignore", but `ls-files -ci --exclude-standard` also honours `.git/info/exclude` and the user's global `core.excludesFile` (`skills/project-update/update.py:1238, 1250`)  in_scope: yes
why it matters: A file ignored only by a per-machine or global rule is reported as a `.gitignore` problem. That is a cosmetic mismatch in the message. The failure is bounded because the hint is read-only.
suggested direction: Say "ignored by git" or "an ignore rule", or leave as is.

findings.label: L3
findings.text:
The hint prints one long line per file with no cap, and the invalid-UTF-8 decode uses `replace` (`skills/project-update/update.py:1245-1254`)  in_scope: yes
why it matters: If a project tracks many ignored files under `.ai/state`, the report floods. Each line repeats about 150 characters of boilerplate. A non-UTF-8 name decodes to U+FFFD, so the printed command points at a path that does not exist. This is an unlikely shape.
suggested direction: Optional. Print the boilerplate once and then the list, or use `os.fsdecode`.

findings.label: L4
findings.text:
The workflow wording is not consistent with the tool text around it (`.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml:4`, line 47)  in_scope: yes
why it matters: The new comment says "four files, five version keys". That matches `FILES` in `tools/sync-version.py`, which lists exactly those four files. But line 47 still says "five version files", and the sync-version docstring says "five places". A reader of the release recipe sees both counts.
suggested direction: Optional wording alignment. The recipe's `git commit -m ... -- <4 files>` is correct, and the path-limited commit also skips unrelated staged changes.

findings.label: I1
findings.text: Nothing further to flag on the scope questions you listed. Details are under EXAMINED AND CLEAN.

findings.label: L4
findings.text: shlex.quote does not stop git pathspec globbing: `git rm --cached -- '<quoted>'` still reads `* ? [ ]` in the name as a glob (default pathspec magic), and the xargs form passes the same names as pathspecs; a tracked-ignored `.ai/state/a[bc].jsonl` or `.ai/state/*` would also untrack matching siblings. Same class as the space defect M1 closes, unpinned. Not executed (the guard refused creating such files under .ai/state) — rests on git's documented pathspec behaviour. Fix direction: `git --literal-pathspecs rm --cached -- …` in both commands (or `:(literal)` prefix), plus one glob-named test case. — skills/project-update/update.py:1253-1254 — in_scope: yes

findings.label: L5
findings.text: The NUL-safe command is broader than the single hint it sits on: it untracks every tracked-ignored file under .ai/state, not just the odd-named one (including ones that also got their own quoted `git rm` hint). It never touches a tracked-but-not-ignored file and the end state is identical to running all hints, so it's acceptable — but the hint text doesn't say "all of them". Fix direction: word the hint accordingly, or accept and note. — skills/project-update/update.py:1254 — in_scope: yes

findings.label: L6
findings.text: The test asserts the command strings only, never executes them; a regression in the NUL-safe command's correctness (flags, pathspec, cwd) would pass. A mutation restoring the raw name, quoting wrong, dropping escaping, or always taking the xargs branch does fail the test, so the "no raw name, no forged line" invariant is pinned. Fix direction (optional): run the printed xargs command in the test repo and assert the index emptied. — tests/test_project_update.py:1463-1486 — in_scope: yes

findings.label: I1
findings.text: Display ambiguity: a literal backslash+`n` (printable) and a real newline both display as `\n`. Harmless: the printable name takes the exact shlex-quoted command, the newline name takes the NUL-safe command, nothing is mis-untracked; cost is only that the escaped display can't tell the user which it is. — skills/project-update/update.py:1252 — in_scope: yes

findings.label: I2
findings.text: The NUL-safe command is cwd-relative, like the old one: `.ai/state` and paths resolve against cwd. From a subdirectory ls-files matches nothing and GNU xargs (no `-r`) runs `git rm --cached --` once with no paths → usage error, never a wrong untrack. For a project nested in a parent work tree, `-C plan.root` lists root-relative paths and the command run from that root is correct; a nested root that isn't its own repo behaves as before. Fails safe; a "run from the project root" note would help. Pre-existing. — skills/project-update/update.py:1254 — in_scope: no
